rationale: Proverb about compelled deference, explicitly introduced by maǧburiye. Searches mənšoq and mənkot yielded no indexed parallel. One attestation; no separate lexical submission sense.

summary: Reviewed all 25 occurrences. Most are ordinary kissing with a body part, a person or an object as patient. Respect, encouragement, supplication and epistolary hand-kissing are contextual functions, not separate numbered senses.
Infectum supports ritual description, a performative greeting and a requested act. The new Detransitive Part. Pass. 102/14 is patient-oriented, contrasting with the active causee construction in III.
Both nšoqo tokens in Talay 1/298 are preserved as separate occurrence decisions for one emphatic repeated Infinitiv construction; the complete existing LB 298 example is not duplicated.
Existing citations overlap PrS 1/68 with prs 5/23 and PrS 6/45 with prs 16/6. Differences of text/verse numbering are questions, not automatic replacements.
No new numbered sense. The Detransitive meaning was already proposed in round 1 from nšəqto; Jan adds its finite Infectum kmənšoqo, not a second Detransitive sense.

Preterit and Infectum reach five cumulative contexts after round 1, and Imperativ has four. Routine hand/eye/person kisses do not need more examples. nšəqleli transparently combines an L-agent and affected-person suffix; do not infer a separate meaning.
Nušaqno ʕaynox at 1.46/2034 is the Turoyo rendering beside Arabic Abus ʕaynək, evidence of a contact greeting. Social deference, farewell and reconciliation remain pragmatic settings of kissing.
Each supplied occurrence has one decision, including both nšəqli tokens at 2.10/2576. The unenumerated second and third nšəqle in 2.18/3747 are not manufactured as additional input records.
Check the inherited 14/15 salutation reference against supplied 14/16, and PrS 1/68 versus prs 5/23; PrS 6/45 versus prs 16/6.
Confirm the detailed morphology of nšəqto at 102/14 against the Detransitive paradigm. Context and the parallel predicate support Part. Pass.; no unseen base form is added.
Is the biting/kissing proverb a fixed shared regional formula? Confirm the finite feminine Detransitive vocalism mənšoqo beside round-1 nšəqto.
Does Nušaqno ʕaynox function as a conventional performative greeting here, with no physical kiss? No separate sense is inferred from the Arabic parallel.

Letters, pictures, a grave and a tree trunk can be literally kissed. They are inanimate patient extensions, not distinct lexical meanings; hand, feet, face and eye-region targets are already represented.
Animal characters as causees retain causative reciprocal kissing and reconciliation, parallel to the inherited human causees.
Reciprocal ḥḏoḏe occurs in prospective farewell, Preterit greeting and an Imperativ reconciliation command. Literal banknote kissing extends round-1 inanimate patients.
